title: Streaming token-level event coalescer and commit semantics for Python SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current Python streaming chat surface emits a flat stream of token and meta events which pushes parsing and coalescing complexity onto application code. Teams building structured output (e.g., JSON partials, tool call frames) need a reliable and ergonomic way to coalesce related token events into higher-level structured events and commit/ack semantics so partial results are usable for downstream processing (telemetry, reranking, storage) without accidental double-processing.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight token-event coalescer in the Python SDK plus an explicit per-request commit/ack API so clients can: 1) receive coalesced structured events (full JSON objects, tool-call blocks, function args) as soon as they're parsable, 2) optionally hold uncommitted interim state and commit only when application-ready, and 3) receive clear resume tokens and idempotency guidance for retries.

Scope:
- SDK surface: new helper ContextManager/EventBatcher plus an incremental "parse_and_commit" primitive on the stream iterator.
- Telemetry hooks: emit coalescer metrics (latency-to-parse, bytes-coalesced) and commit events.
- Backpressure: surface a non-blocking soft-signal to the runtime to reduce burst size when client is slow to commit.

Non-goals:
- Not adding server-side language-model changes (this is client-side coalescing only).
- Not changing transport protocol or token framing from the service; relies on existing streaming wire events.

Example usage (RFC prototype):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
from redwood.streaming import EventBatcher

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
stream = client.stream_chat(model="rwd-3b", messages=conversation)

with EventBatcher(stream) as batches:
    for batch in batches:  # yields coalesced logical events ("json_object", "tool_frame", "partial_text")
        if batch.type == "json_object":
            data = batch.parsed  # completed JSON from multiple token events
            # application can inspect before committing
            if validate(data):
                batch.commit()  # idempotent commit signal; emits commit telemetry
            else:
                batch.abort()   # release buffered tokens and mark as dropped

Notes: commit() is local/SDK-level and emits a checkpoint token clients may persist. On retry the server will re-stream tokens but the SDK uses the persisted checkpoint to dedupe up to commit point.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes EventBatcher context manager that yields coalesced logical events
Commit/abort API present and documented; commit returns stable checkpoint token string
Unit tests cover nested JSON partials, interleaved tool frames, and aborted batches
Benchmarked coalescer overhead < 2% CPU on representative 2k token streams
Telemetry emitted for parse latency, commit rate, aborted batches; visible in Console dev route
design_notes: Coalescer works as a streaming state machine: collects token fragments until a deterministic parse boundary is found (balanced braces for JSON, end-of-tool marker for tool frames).
Avoid deep JSON parsing on every token: incremental chunked parser (based on Python's json.JSONDecoder with a small custom buffer) to detect complete objects with bounded lookahead.
Checkpoint token is a SDK-generated id + last-server-offset tuple; stored as opaque string for apps. Server need not understand it.
Backpressure: coalescer keeps a soft buffer limit (default 64KB). When exceeded, SDK raises a 'soft stall' signal to internal runtime to reduce batch size; not a hard throw to user code.
Edge cases: malformed partial JSON must be surfaced as 'parse_error' batch with raw tokens available for debugging; not auto-aborted.
decisions: Use SDK-side checkpointing (opted for simplicity) instead of requiring server-provided resume tokens (avoids server changes).
Expose both blocking and non-blocking commit: commit() (sync) and try_commit() (returns False if runtime still flushing).
Metric names standardized: rwd.sdk.coalescer.parse_latency_ms, rwd.sdk.coalescer.bytes_buffered, rwd.sdk.coalescer.committed_batches.
tradeoffs: Client-side checkpointing is opportunistic: reduces server work but may replay tokens on resumed connections. Opted for clear API and simplicity over perfect dedupe guarantees.

Incremental JSON detection uses lightweight heuristics (brace counting) which may false-positive on strings containing braces; we mitigate by attempting a parse only when heuristic indicates boundary and falling back to full parse with error reporting.
Inserting coalescer increases SDK complexity and testing surface area; benefits: much simpler app code and better telemetry.
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype EventBatcher and incremental parser; write unit tests for JSON and tool-frame detection.
Week 2: integrate commit/abort checkpoint generation and local persistence helpers; add telemetry hooks.
Week 3: e2e tests against recorded streams; perf microbenchmarks and tune buffer thresholds.
Week 4: docs + examples (cookbook) + release candidate; solicit SDK maintainers review; ship in release python-sdk-2026.03-RC1
